unit: Paul Irving came from Boston to Avonlea to live with his grandmother, Grandma Irving, three years after his mother passed away. He attended the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley, with whom he instantly formed a bond as a kindred spirit and favorite pupil. During his schooldays, he got along well with his peers, even fighting a drawn battle with St. Clair Donnell to defend the American flag and harboring a childhood crush on Gracie Andrews. He regularly struggled with eating the generous helpings of porridge served by his grandmother, though he eventually began growing rapidly. Paul also enjoyed visits to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge; he later welcomed his father Stephen Irving's return and their eventual marriage, calling Miss Lavendar 'Mother Lavendar'. As he grew older, he moved to Boston with his family, traded his fairy fancies for sports like football, and developed a talent for writing poetry that earned magazine publication. He drove the carriage for Anne and Gilbert Blythe on their wedding day and wrote a lyric about a bird singing during their ceremony. Later, he made plans to go abroad for two years of study.
